title: Online retail market to cross $90b in 2026 with grocery overtaking mobiles: Redseer
content: India's online retail market is projected to cross $90 billion in 2026, registering an annual growth of 22-24%, its fastest expansion in five years, driven by everyday consumption categories such as grocery rather than mobile phones, Redseer Strategy Consultants said in a report. According to the analysis, ecommerce gross merchandise value (GMV) expanded roughly 25% year-on-year to about $38 billion in the first half (H1) of 2026, marking its strongest H1 performance in four years. While online retail accelerated, mobile sales remained flat at 0% growth during the first half and are projected to grow by just 2-3% across the full year due to sharp price increases curbing sales volumes. Consequently, the grocery segment is poised to overtake mobile phones as the second-largest category in Indian ecommerce, behind fashion. "This year, India's online retail is growing fastest where demand is steadiest," said Kushal Bhatnagar, Partner at Redseer. The report noted that grocery, beauty and personal care (BPC), and home and furniture will account for about 40% of overall online retail GMV in 2026 and roughly three-fifths of the incremental GMV added during the year. Grocery alone is projected to account for nearly a third of the added GMV, expanding 50-53% for the full year and lifting its market share from 16% in 2025 to 19% in 2026. Mobiles, which accounted for around 19% of total sales last year, are expected to see their market share drop to roughly 16%. BPC is projected to rise 36-39%, while home and furniture is estimated to expand 31-34% in 2026. In contrast, electronics experienced a 22% rebound in H1 2026 after contracting 5% in the corresponding period of 2025. Redseer attributed this spike to "pre-loaded" demand, spurred by the reduction of goods and services tax (GST) on large appliances from 28% to 18% in September 2025, heavy discounting on air conditioners due to changes in Bureau of Energy Efficiency star ratings, an LPG shortage driving a 200–300% surge in induction cooktops, and early laptop purchases ahead of expected component price increases.

title: Hunar.AI raises Rs 40 Cr in Series A funding round led by Blume Ventures
content: Hunar.AI has raised Rs 40 crore in a Series A funding round led by Blume Ventures. The round also saw participation from Hyderabad Angels Fund, Together Fund, Seedstars, AVNM Ventures, PhysicsWallah co-founders Prateek Maheshwari and Alakh Pandey, and MediaMint co-founder Aditya Vuchi. Hunar.AI will use the funds for building AI infrastructure, product development, and go-to-market expansion. The company is focused on developing specialised AI technology for frontline-intensive industries, where high-volume hiring, geographically distributed teams, and language diversity create operational challenges that conventional HR systems struggle to address. “Frontline workforce management is one of the largest yet most underserved opportunities in enterprise AI. Solving it requires more than applying general-purpose models to existing processes. It demands a deep understanding of industry workflows, multilingual capabilities and technology that can reliably execute tasks at scale,” said Krishna Khandelwal, Co-founder and CEO, Hunar.AI. Founded in 2022 by Krishna Khandelwal and Shantanu Bhattacharyya, Hunar’s platform comprises Hunar Voice and Hunar Connect, which use conversational AI agents to manage workforce workflows through voice, WhatsApp and chat. Workflows include candidate sourcing and screening, interview scheduling, onboarding, training, employee engagement and worker retention. By automating high-volume interactions, the platform helps enterprises manage frontline workforce processes while maintaining communication with candidates and employees across locations. Arpit Agrawal, Partner at Blume Ventures said, “As the world looks to India for lessons in managing these new-age businesses at scale, Hunar is building the AI layer that makes them possible. By focusing on outcomes rather than infrastructure, Hunar has the potential to build a category in India that can scale globally.” According to a statement, Hunar’s AI agents handled over 15 million conversations in September 2026, with conversation volumes doubling every quarter. Its clients include Swiggy, Delhivery, Instamart, Pronto, Blue Dart, Flipkart, Aditya Birla Capital and Tata Croma. NITI Aayog projects that India’s gig workforce will grow from around 1 crore workers in 2024–25 to 2.35 crore by 2029–30. As enterprises expand across cities and regions, hiring, onboarding and retaining workers efficiently has become an important operational priority, with many processes still dependent on manual calls, repeated follow-ups and coordination.

title: Eloelo's Saurabh Pandey bets that Dolphin AI can break the gatekeepers of Indian storytelling
content: When James Cameron's epic sci-fi movie Avatar hit cinemas in late 2000s, plenty of Indians watched it and wondered why we weren't making films like that. According to Saurabh Pandey, Founder and CEO of Eloelo Group, that question is about to lose its force. Eloelo is an Indian live social entertainment and social gaming platform headquartered in Bengaluru. It was launched in 2020 by former Flipkart executives Pandey and Akshay Dubey. The platform bridges video/audio livestreaming with interactive gaming tailored specifically for India's youth and vernacular markets. At the 17th edition of TechSparks, YourStory's flagship event, Pandey showed off Dolphin AI, Eloelo's AI video creation tool, in a session titled 'Can AI turn India into a global content export hub?', moderated by Shradha Sharma, Founder and CEO of YourStory and The Bharat Project. Dolphin AI currently has a waitlist, with the platform releasing invite codes in batches. For now, Dolphin AI is free as Eloelo is giving away generous early credits so creators can make their first few videos and get a feel for the solution. However, a credit-based pricing model will arrive eventually. Pandey said the team mainly wants to see how people use Dolphin AI, and early signs are promising: roughly 15,000 videos were built in about eight days, mostly through organic discovery. The end of the budget bottleneck Pandey's pitch centres on who gets to tell big stories. In the VFX era, he said, movie making belonged to whoever had the money. A good storyteller with a period drama in mind simply could not afford the visuals it demanded, and that made budgets the real gatekeeper of content. AI is a total game-changer, he argued. Production usually eats up 50 to 60% of revenue in this category, squeezing distribution budgets and destroying unit economics. By slashing those production costs, creator imagination finally gets the breathing room it needs to thrive. Distribution, meanwhile, has become largely algorithmic. A creator in India now competes for attention in the US or Europe on the same footing as anyone else. Why this time might be different The conversation then moved to another area of content that is seeing traction: micro-drama and short-form content. These have attracted plenty of Indian startups, yet few have become popular. In India, he said, the top four or five micro-drama players together are running at more than Rs 5,000 crore, a level they reached in just 18 months. He also pointed to South Korea, a country of 52 million people that has built a $15-billion content export economy. India has 1.4 billion people and no shortage of creative talent, he said. What it has lacked is intent, technology, ambition and capital. Too many Indian creators, in his view, still focus only on local audience. Nobody asks whether a new LLM is launching for India, he noted; it just launches for the world. Why shouldn't Indian stories do the same? Platforms will consolidate, but supply is wide open Pandey doesn't expect micro-drama to escape the pattern seen elsewhere. Food delivery, quick commerce, ecommerce and ride-hailing all ended up with two or three heavily funded players holding 70 to 75% of the market, and he expects the same for content. The real opportunity, he said, lies on the supply side. Eloelo launched about 200 new micro-dramas last month, roughly five or six a night, and works with around 90 production houses. His advice to would-be founders is to skip the platform race and build lean AI studios instead: a handful of writers, editors, promo producers and a line producer who could feed micro-dramas, OTT content and exportable IP to the big platforms. He also had a message for writers and producers wary of AI. Use it as a brainstorming partner, he said, and ship more. As an example, he floated an idea close to his heart. An AI Ramayana already exists, but nobody has yet made a spectacular AI Mahabharata. Eloelo has grown from one platform to five within the same group, Pandey said, and an IPO is not on the cards anytime soon. The focus is on growing profitably and sustainably.

title: How a FD calculator helps investors plan savings with ease
content: Establishing a financial goal makes the process of saving a lot easier. If you plan to save well, you need to know the total amount you plan to save as well as the time frame for saving. Whether you want to save for a family event, pay for tuition, or renovate your home, you should be aware of the amount of money you want to save and the time frame. A fixed deposit is a type of investment that guarantees you a fixed amount of return during the investment period. However, calculating returns manually can be a hassle. So, using Bajaj Finance's FD Calculator saves a lot of time and energy as it allows you to know your estimated returns in seconds based on your inputs. You can explore options before making the final investment. Define your savings goal The first crucial step in investing is to find out your investment's purpose. Knowing why you are making the investment will give you the desired amount you need to save and the time of retrieval for the money. For example, if the amount required for a particular instance is Rs 3 lakh in three years, you can use the calculator See how much your deposit may earn The Bajaj Finance FD Calculator estimates your return after you provide the required inputs. These generally include the investment amount, investor category, tenure, and interest payout option. The result shows the estimated interest earned and the expected maturity amount. This allows you to see how much of the final value comes from your original deposit and how much may come from interest. The calculation also makes percentage rates easier to understand. An annual interest rate may appear attractive, but the calculator translates it into an estimated rupee value. This provides a more practical picture of how the investment could contribute towards your savings goal. Choose an amount without affecting your budget A larger amount will yield a higher maturity value, but putting in too much money could create issues when it's time to pay the bills. The right figure would give you the money you need to achieve your future goal. Before making a fixed deposit, be sure to think about rent, bills, school tuition, medical expenses, and anything else that you must pay for in the near future. The calculator allows you to compare various amounts almost instantly. Enter Rs 50,000, Rs 1 lakh, or any other amount and watch the maturity figure change accordingly. Match the tenure with your goal date Bajaj Finance’s fixed deposit scheme has time frames that range from 12 to 60 months. The applicable interest rate differs based on the time chosen, meaning changing the time can result in varied rates of return. A longer period gives the deposit a longer opportunity to earn interest through the compound option, but maturity needs to happen close to the time of using the funds. Suppose your goal is due after two years. Selecting a five-year deposit merely because it shows a larger maturity value could leave the funds unavailable at the required time. The FD interest Calculator lets you compare eligible tenures and select one that balances potential earnings with timely access. How to use the FD calculator The Bajaj Finance online calculator is designed to provide estimates quickly. You can repeat the calculation with different inputs and compare the results before starting the investment process. Select the tenure: Choose an available period between 12 and 60 months. Pick the payout option: Select interest at maturity or a periodic payout frequency. Review the estimate: Check the estimated interest earnings and maturity amount. Try another combination: Change the amount, tenure, or payout option to compare the result. Consider safety and access to your money Return is only one aspect of FD planning. Credit ratings of the institution, conditions for early withdrawal, nomination facility, maturity instructions, and renewal options are some other aspects that must be evaluated as well. Bajaj Finance Fixed Deposit comes with guaranteed returns and good credit safety ratings, with CRISIL AAA/STABLE and ICRA AAA (Stable). Minimum investment starts at Rs 15,000, making it possible to experiment with various amounts via the calculator before finalizing the exact amount. Early withdrawals are allowed but require certain conditions to be met, which could lead to lower interest. Therefore, it is wise to select an amount and tenure you are fairly certain you will not deviate from. The Bajaj Finance FD Calculator lets you know the returns that different fixed deposit accounts can bring. It is useful to compare various investment scenarios involving the fixed deposit calculator and check information about current FD interest rates, tax rates, credit ratings, and penalties for early withdrawal of a fixed deposit. title: 5 Quotes from the book It Matters a Lot by Shubhra Saxena
content: We spend much of our lives working towards milestones that society considers important. Degrees, careers, financial security, relationships and recognition often become measures of success. But what happens when we achieve these goals and still feel that something is missing? This is one of the central questions explored in It Matters A Lot by Shubhra Saxena, an IAS officer and author. Published by Rupa Publications, the book examines identity, ambition, happiness, relationships, failure and the experiences that shape how we understand ourselves. Rather than prescribing a universal formula for a meaningful life, Saxena encourages readers to question their assumptions and reflect on what genuinely matters to them. 5 Thought-provoking quotes from the book 1. “Because you can tick every box and still miss your own life.” This line captures the central message of It Matters A Lot . We often follow a familiar checklist for success, pursuing educational qualifications, professional achievements, financial stability and personal milestones without stopping to question whether these goals reflect our own desires. The problem is not ambition itself. Working towards something meaningful can bring satisfaction and purpose. However, when our goals are shaped entirely by external expectations, we may lose sight of what makes us happy. Saxena invites readers to consider whether they are building a life that feels right to them or simply one that looks successful to everyone else. The lesson: Achievement and fulfilment are not always the same. A meaningful life begins with understanding what success means to you. 2. “You can tick every box and still feel like something is missing.” This line explores the gap between outward success and inner contentment. A person may have a stable career, a comfortable lifestyle and relationships that appear ideal, yet still struggle to understand why they feel unfulfilled. Such feelings can arise when we pursue goals without examining the reasons behind them. We may believe that the next promotion, purchase or milestone will finally bring happiness, only to discover that the feeling does not last. It Matters A Lot encourages readers to look beyond achievements and examine their emotional needs, values and expectations. The lesson: Before chasing another milestone, pause and ask yourself what you hope it will bring into your life. Sometimes, understanding that desire matters more than achieving the goal. 3. “What happens when everything looks right and still doesn't feel enough?” This question reflects a familiar struggle in a world that encourages constant comparison . Social media, professional competition and cultural expectations can make us feel that we are falling behind, even when we have made meaningful progress. The difficulty is that there is always another achievement to pursue and another person against whom to measure ourselves. If our satisfaction depends entirely on reaching the next milestone, contentment can remain perpetually out of reach. Saxena's book encourages readers to reconsider these expectations and develop a more personal understanding of happiness and fulfilment. The lesson: You do not have to keep pursuing every goal that society celebrates. Learning to recognise what is enough for you can be just as important as striving for more. 4. “Why do we seek approval?” The desire for approval can influence our decisions more than we realise. From choosing a career to navigating relationships, we may find ourselves prioritising other people's opinions over our own judgement. Seeking acceptance is a natural human experience. Problems arise when external validation becomes the primary measure of our worth. We may begin making decisions to avoid criticism rather than to pursue what genuinely matters to us. By encouraging readers to examine their beliefs and motivations, It Matters A Lot opens the door to greater self-awareness and more conscious choices. The lesson: Other people's opinions can offer useful perspectives, but they do not have to determine the direction of your life. Understanding your values can help you make decisions with greater confidence. Also Read Shubhra Saxena’s It Matters A Lot: 5 Lessons on conscious living 5. “What are we really looking for in love, ambition, happiness, and success?” These questions bring together several of the themes explored throughout It Matters A Lot . We often pursue different things without examining what we expect them to provide. We may seek success because we want security, relationships because we want connection , or recognition because we want to feel valued. Yet the things we pursue and the needs we hope to fulfil are not always the same. Taking time to understand these motivations can help us recognise unhelpful patterns and make choices that better reflect our priorities. The lesson: Self-awareness begins when we become curious about our own desires. Asking honest questions can help us understand not only what we want, but why we want it. Final thoughts It Matters A Lot by Shubhra Saxena invites readers to reconsider the assumptions that shape their understanding of a successful and meaningful life. Its central message is that achievements alone cannot determine whether we feel fulfilled. Through questions about identity, ambition, relationships and happiness, the book encourages readers to pause and reflect on the lives they are building. Perhaps the most important question is not whether we have achieved everything we once wanted, but whether the life we are living reflects what truly matters to us.

title: 5 Richard Osman quotes that reveal the human side of mystery
content: Mystery novels are often associated with murder, hidden clues, unexpected suspects and shocking revelations. But the most memorable crime stories are not always about discovering who committed a crime. Sometimes, they are about understanding why people behave the way they do, what they hide from others and what they need most from life. British author Richard Osman explores these themes in his bestselling crime fiction, particularly The Thursday Murder Club. The novel follows four older residents of a retirement community who investigate unsolved murders, bringing together suspense, humour, friendship and reflections on ageing. What makes Osman's writing appealing is the way ordinary human experiences sit alongside extraordinary crimes. His characters have regrets, complicated relationships, personal ambitions and a deep desire to feel connected to others. 5 Richard Osman quotes that reveal the human side of mystery 1. “I know the difference between alone and lonely” This line from The Thursday Murder Club captures an important distinction between solitude and loneliness. Being alone does not necessarily mean feeling isolated. Some people genuinely enjoy their own company, while others can feel lonely even when surrounded by friends, family or colleagues. The difference lies in whether solitude is a choice or an experience that leaves someone feeling disconnected. Osman's characters challenge the assumption that older people naturally become less interested in the world around them. They continue to seek companionship, excitement, intellectual stimulation and opportunities to make a difference. The quote also reminds readers that meaningful relationships are not simply about having people nearby. They are about feeling understood, valued and included. The takeaway: Loneliness is not always visible. A person can have a busy social life and still long for a deeper connection with someone who understands them. 2. “We all want to be chosen” In The Thursday Murder Club, Osman explores the complicated relationship between choice, belonging and the desire to be wanted. The novel's reflections on this subject are collected among its widely shared quotations. The desire to be chosen appears in many aspects of life. People want to be selected for opportunities, appreciated by friends, loved by partners and remembered by those who matter to them. Even people who appear independent may quietly wonder whether they are important to anyone else. This is one reason mysteries can be so emotionally engaging. Beneath the investigation, characters may be struggling with rejection, insecurity, jealousy or the fear of becoming irrelevant. Their actions become easier to understand when readers look beyond the evidence and consider their emotional needs. Osman's characters demonstrate that the need for acceptance does not disappear with age. It remains part of being human, regardless of experience or social status. The takeaway: Wanting to matter to someone is not a weakness. The important thing is to recognise your worth without allowing other people's approval to define it. 3. “Count the good days” Osman's writing frequently balances the darker elements of crime fiction with observations about appreciating everyday life. In The Thursday Murder Club, this idea appears in a reflection about recognising good days and carrying their memories forward. Crime stories often revolve around loss, uncertainty and the consequences of past decisions. Yet these difficult circumstances can make ordinary pleasures feel more meaningful. A conversation with a friend, a shared meal or a peaceful afternoon can become precious when life feels unpredictable. The residents of Coopers Chase have lived long enough to understand that happiness does not always arrive through dramatic achievements. Sometimes, it comes from small moments of companionship and the freedom to enjoy the present. This perspective gives Osman's mysteries an emotional depth that goes beyond solving crimes. Readers are encouraged to notice the good in their own lives rather than waiting for everything to become perfect. The takeaway: Not every day needs to be extraordinary to be worthwhile. Learning to appreciate small moments can change how we remember our lives. 4. “Always look where the action isn't” This observation from The Thursday Murder Club reflects the attention to detail that makes a good detective. In a mystery, the most obvious suspect is not necessarily the person responsible. A convincing investigation requires looking beyond dramatic events and paying attention to the details that others overlook. The same principle applies to understanding people. Someone's loudest reaction may not reveal their deepest concern, while a quiet change in behaviour can suggest that something important is happening beneath the surface. Osman's approach to crime fiction places considerable emphasis on character. In an interview with PBS Books, he explained that he begins with his characters and develops the murder plot around them. This approach encourages readers to become observers of human behaviour rather than simply followers of clues. The takeaway: Important truths are not always found in the most obvious places. Sometimes, listening carefully and noticing what others miss can reveal more than making quick assumptions. 5. “Don't let it be in charge” Osman's observations about everyday life also extend to money and the influence it can have on personal decisions. A short line from The Thursday Murder Club captures this idea: “Don't let it be in charge.” Although the novel is a murder mystery, its characters encounter concerns that extend well beyond crime. Money, relationships, family responsibilities and personal independence all shape how people navigate the world. Financial security can provide freedom and comfort, but the pursuit of money can also influence priorities, create conflict and complicate relationships. When material success becomes the only measure of achievement, other sources of happiness can be overlooked. This theme also connects to the wider appeal of Osman's characters: they are not defined by a single ambition or social role. They have different motivations, values and ideas about what makes life meaningful. The takeaway: Money can be an important tool, but it should not become the sole measure of a successful life. Personal relationships, peace of mind and a sense of purpose matter too. Final thoughts Richard Osman’s mysteries blend crime and humour with thoughtful insights into loneliness, friendship, ageing and belonging. The Thursday Murder Club resonates because its characters face familiar emotional struggles. Ultimately, the human side of a mystery is what gives its revelations lasting meaning. Discovering who committed a crime may resolve the central puzzle, but understanding the people involved is what makes the story memorable.

title: The science of deep sleep and how Duroflex Airboost helps you get more of it
content: You can get enough sleep and still not get enough recovery. We obsess over sleep duration, the “eight hours” metric, but duration alone doesn't tell the whole story. What matters just as much is depth. Deep sleep is the stage where the body does its heaviest lifting: repairing tissue, consolidating memory, and resetting the hormones that govern everything from appetite to stress. Yet for a growing number of people, deep sleep is the first thing to go missing, even when total sleep time looks normal on paper. The different stages of sleep Sleep isn't a single, uniform state. It cycles through distinct stages roughly every 90 minutes, each with a different job. Light sleep (N1 and N2) acts as the transition zone; the body slows down, heart rate drops, and brain activity shifts into slower rhythms. This stage makes up the bulk of a typical night, but it's largely preparatory. Deep sleep, or N3 stage (also called slow-wave sleep), is where the real restorative work happens. Brain waves slow dramatically, blood pressure and breathing reach their lowest points, and the body redirects energy toward physical repair, regenerating muscle, strengthening the immune system, and clearing metabolic waste from the brain. Growth hormone release peaks during this stage, which is why it's often called the body's “repair shift”, Rapid Eye Movement(REM) sleep stage follows, associated more with dreaming and cognitive processing than physical recovery. Crucially, deep sleep is front-loaded into the first half of the night. If you go to bed late, cut sleep short, or microawake multiple times during your sleep, you disproportionately lose N3 stage, even if your total hours stay roughly the same. When eight hours still isn’t enough If you’re usually sleep-deprived, you don’t get to know it right away, since it doesn't show itself with obvious symptoms. Most of these symptoms are considered normal and ignorable, like sluggish mornings, feeling tired, and being unproductive. But the sleep debt compounds, and it can affect your physical recovery, leading to muscle soreness, joint stiffness, and lingering fatigue. It can also affect your overall immunity, since much of the body’s repair and defence activity happens mostly during the N3 stage. Without enough N3 stage in every sleep cycle, it becomes harder to regulate your hormones, including the balance of cortisol and growth hormone, which can affect stress resilience, appetite, and long-term metabolic health. Your cognitive sharpness also takes a hit, since deep sleep (N3 stage) also plays a role in clearing metabolic wastes from the brain overnight. Heat discomfort, spinal misalignment, and micro-awakenings during the night can prevent the body from settling into and staying in N3, even across a full eight hours in bed. Many people don’t realise that the frustrating part isn’t always how many hours you sleep, but how much of the right kind of sleep you’re actually getting. Where Duroflex Airboost mattress comes in Duroflex Airboost was engineered specifically to support quicker sleep onset and deeper sleep, positioning itself as India's newest sleep technology built around this problem. Airboost is Duroflex's proprietary open-matrix mattress technology, built from over one lakh independently responsive fibres designed to improve airflow, movement response, and postural support. Trusted by athletes around the world, this sleep technology is brought to Indiab for the first time by Duroflex. Airboost is accredited by the Indian Society for Sleep Research (ISSR) and recommended by doctors at the National Health Academy (NHA). Three features built around deep sleep 1. Pressure relief from postural support Rather than offering uniform support across the body, the mattress uses hyperlocal support built from over one lakh+ AirKnit fibres, distributing pressure according to the body's actual contours. You get the right kind of postural alignment for all types of sleepers as the individual fibres easily support every tiny pressure point across your body. Misalignment and pressure build-up at the shoulders and hips are a common reason sleepers wake or shift position before completing a full deep-sleep cycle; proper medium-firm support like this addresses the issue at the source rather than masking it with extra foam cushioning. 2. An open-matrix core for breathability Airboost features a 3D open-cell matrix made up of roughly 90% air, creating continuous airflow throughout the mattress that helps dissipate heat and sweat more effectively, keeping sleepers closer to a thermoneutral zone for cooler, deeper sleep. Airboost is 3X more breathable than traditional mattresses on the market. Since body temperature naturally needs to drop to initiate and sustain deep sleep, a surface that actively supports heat dissipation removes one of the most common, and least discussed, barriers to N3 sleep. 3. Energy restoration Each Airboost fibre responds instantly to the pressure placed on it, providing maximum rebound that makes turning and changing positions effortless. This way, the body’s energy is conserved for overnight recovery and you get to complete full sleep cycles without micro-awakenings. Frequent, effortful repositioning is one of the quiet disruptors of deep sleep; every restless shift is a small pull away from the N3 stage. By minimizing these and micro-awakenings, this mattress helps the body stay in deep sleep for longer, uninterrupted stretches. Airboost is accredited by the Indian Society for Sleep Research (ISSR) for delivering 30% more deep sleep(N3 stage), and is also recommended by doctors at the National Health Academy (NHA). Rather than treating sleep as one undifferentiated block of hours, their design specifically targets enhancement of N3 sleep, the stage most essential for physical repair, stronger immunity, and stress recovery. Final thoughts The conversation around sleep is shifting, from counting hours to increasing sleep stages. Deep sleep isn't a luxury metric; it's the mechanism behind physical recovery, immune resilience, and hormonal balance. As awareness grows, so does scrutiny of the products claiming to support it. Duroflex Airboost , a combination of engineered airflow, responsive movement support, and clinically backed deep-sleep enhancement, reflects a broader shift in the mattress category, one where design decisions are increasingly expected to be measured, not just marketed.
