title: UP cabinet approves startup procurement scheme
content: The Uttar Pradesh Cabinet has approved the Uttar Pradesh Startup Procurement Scheme - 2026. The scheme aims to facilitate market access for eligible startups in the state and promote the use of their innovative products, services and solutions by government departments and other agencies, the UP government said in a statement. Under the scheme, a dedicated UP Startup E-Marketplace will be established to list innovative products, services and solutions developed by eligible startups and facilitate their procurement by government departments. This platform will enable government departments to procure innovative products and services offered by startups. The departments will make purchases from their approved budgetary provisions. The Uttar Pradesh Startup Mission will be responsible for establishing, operating and maintaining the UP Startup E-Marketplace, ensuring its continued implementation. The wider use of these technological solutions will improve the quality, efficiency and accessibility of government services. Citizens will directly benefit from better, more effective and accessible service delivery. Under the scheme, eligible innovative enterprises registered under the Uttar Pradesh Startup Policy will also have opportunities to secure work orders from government departments. Access to government procurement opportunities will encourage business expansion among startups and generate additional direct and indirect employment opportunities in the state, the statement added. The Uttar Pradesh government also approved a skill training and employment development scheme to make the state a key sourcing hub for skilled manpower and a “global manpower hub”. The Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel Skill Training and Employment Zone Development Scheme was approved by the state cabinet. Under the scheme, it will develop an integrated skill training and employment ecosystem across nine zones, covering all 75 districts. This will help train young people to meet industry requirements and connect them with employment opportunities in India and abroad. The Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME) sector plays an important role in Uttar Pradesh's industrial development. The state has approximately 96 lakh MSME enterprises, accounting for 14.2 per cent of the country's approximately 6.77 crore enterprises.

title: Amazon, Flipkart see strong start to 2026 festive sales
content: India’s two largest ecommerce platforms, Amazon India and Flipkart, have launched their flagship annual festive sales—the Amazon Great Indian Festival (GIF) 2026 and Flipkart’s The Big Billion Days (TBBD) 2026. Both platforms reported strong consumer participation, sharp increase in demand across categories, and growing adoption of quick-commerce delivery options in non-metro markets. Scale, traffic, and reach Amazon said it recorded over 440 million visits during the opening phase of its sale, the highest volume in its history. The platform saw a 100% year-on-year increase in products ordered, while daily app downloads surged fivefold. More than 72% of visits came from outside the top nine metros. First-time shoppers nearly doubled year-on-year, and orders were placed from every pin code in the country. Flipkart, meanwhile, recorded 6.3 million concurrent users per minute during its opening peak hour, attracting over six times as many active users as during a regular hour. The platform said it also recorded 287 million sessions during the early access window for Plus, Black, and co-branded card members. Non-metro markets accounted for approximately 60% of overall traction, with Tier III towns and beyond contributing nearly half of all visits during the opening hour, it said. New customer numbers grew 34% during the same period. Category drivers and shopping trends Amazon said electronics and premium upgrades performed exceptionally well. Premium Android smartphone sales rose 70% year-on-year, while MacBook Neo sales grew 65X over a regular business day. Large appliances surged 50X, led by washing machines (80X), refrigerators (60X), and home entertainment (77X). In fashion, footwear sales reached seven pairs per second, while Nike sales rose 16-fold compared with regular days. Denim sales exceeded 1,500 pairs per hour, while premium beauty products sold at a rate of 150 units per minute. Flipkart said it saw strong demand in Large Appliances, which grew 30% year-on-year in the first hour, alongside a 73% year-on-year jump in tablets. Beauty sales on Flipkart grew 42% overall and 48% among Gen Z shoppers, heavily propelled by men's grooming. At peak, Flipkart said it processed over 1,600 units of men's perfume every minute. On the engagement side, over 12.7 million users accessed Flipkart’s live commerce and video shopping experiences, while 64% of Voice Search users came from Tier II plus markets. Quick commerce and digital payment adoption Rapid fulfillment became a central battleground across both marketplaces. Amazon said it fulfilled orders within minutes across more than 120 cities served by Amazon Now. Flipkart Minutes saw order volumes rise 3.5X over normal days and new customers jump 11X in the first hour, highlighted by a record delivery of an iPhone 17 to a customer in New Delhi in 3.4 minutes. Affordability levers drove high-ticket conversion across both platforms. Half of Amazon’s buyers utilised EMI options, while Amazon Pay Later saw transactions double and its user base expand by 80% year-on-year. Flipkart similarly reported that one in three mobile buyers opted for No Cost EMI, while one in four utilized product exchange offers. Merchant ecosystem and brand traction Seller participation expanded across both platforms. Amazon said sellers recorded over 2X units ordered in the first 24 hours compared to last year, with sellers generating over Rs 1 crore in sales growing by more than 80%. Category growth for sellers was led by beauty (7X), kitchen (4.2X), and wireless (3.4X). Some of the key partner brands reported significant surges such as Philips (10X over daily baseline), Reebok (doubled sales YoY), WROGN (10X over daily baseline), and Penguin Random House India (up nearly 50% YoY). Flipkart said reported that 51% of transacting sellers doubled their standard daily business during Early Access. Sellers based in Tier II plus regions such as small businesses and MSMEs achieved a 2.9X growth, with manufacturing and seller hubs such as Bhiwandi, Panipat, Tirupur, and Hisar leading the sales momentum.

title: Lalit Kala Akademi features 270 artworks in its 65th National Exhibition of Art
content: Launched in 2014, PhotoSparks is a weekly feature from YourStory, with photographs that celebrate the spirit of creativity and innovation. In the earlier 1,020 posts, we featured an art festival , cartoon gallery . world music festival , telecom expo , millets fair , climate change expo , wildlife conference , startup festival , Diwali rangoli , and jazz festival . Lalit Kala Akademi (LKA) in New Delhi is celebrating its 65th National Exhibition of Art this year, featuring over 270 artworks from around the country. For over six decades, India's National Academy of Art has provided a platform for contemporary artistic expression. As seen in this photo essay, the exhibition celebrates the creative excellence of Indian artists and reflects the evolving visual culture of Indian traditions and contemporary practices. It showcases creativity from diverse regions, materials, mediums, themes, and styles. Also Read Year in Review: The great Indian consumer reset powered by protein, pickleball and micro-dramas The cultural plurality is reflected across core concepts such as spirituality, nature, society, remembrance, and open interpretation. The artists explore connections between the personal and the collective, the traditional and the contemporary. The showcase is more than an annual exhibition—it is a reminder of the importance of diversity and unity in the country. Viewers from India and overseas are inspired by the shared values and cultural imagination of a living civilisation with ancient roots. The organisers reportedly received 6,175 artworks from 2,495 artists, representing 27 States and Union Territories. A rigorous selection process presented 270 artworks for the exhibition. Also Read Year in Review: Top 10 celebrity-backed ventures of 2025 Another jury process selected 20 artworks by 20 artists for the Lalit Kala Akademi Awards. The winners included Chandra Shekhar Sain, Gopal Chandra Naskar, Kishor Kumar Narkhadiwala, Mrinal Dey, Nidhi Chopra, Nimai Singh Sarungbam, and Pankaj Kumar Sharma. Some of the artworks are also available for acquisition. This offers a direct economic channel between artists, collectors and the public. Lalit Kala Akademi was inaugurated on August 5, 1954 by then Education Minister Maulana Abul Kalam Azad. Its activities include documentation of Indian art and creating platforms for exhibitions, research and artistic exchange. Also Read Breaking barriers in 2025: Women’s progress at work and what the road ahead demands In addition to the central hub in Delhi, there are regional offices in Chennai, Kolkata, Bhubaneswar, Agartala, Shimla, Patna, Ahmedabad. They provide a range of scholarships, studios and artist programmes. LKA maintains a significant permanent collection documenting the diversity of modern, contemporary, folk, and tribal art in India. Examples include Bengal's scroll traditions, southern sculpture practices, and the distinctive artistic traditions of the North-East. For artists, being featured at the exhibition provides national visibility and institutional recognition. For audiences, it offers a broad survey of current artistic practices across geographical and stylistic boundaries. Also Read How IIT Madras Incubation Cell is powering India’s next-gen deeptech startups This photo essay showcases some of the outstanding works of painting, sculpture, photography. and mixed media. Other exhibitis are in bronze, terracotta, ceramic, wood, stone, and marble. Together, the 270 artworks reflect how the annual national exhibition is particularly important because it operates at the intersection of artist recognition, national cultural policy, and the contemporary Indian art ecosystem. Now what have you done today to pause in your busy schedule and harness your creative side for a better world? (All photographs taken by Madanmohan Rao on location at Lalit Kala Akademi.)

title: ShuruKar: Your next business could start in your hometown
content: A big idea does not need a big city. That was the message from Patna, where The Bharat Project, an initiative by YourStory , launched ShuruKar at Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam Science City in Rajinder Nagar. Developed in partnership with DPIIT and Startup India, ShuruKar is billed as the first nationwide district-level movement of its kind. It aims to help young Indians identify a problem worth solving in their district, build a business around it, and continue growing it. The launch drew Shri Nitish Mishra, Minister, Urban Development and Housing Department, Government of Bihar, along with founders, students and young entrepreneurs from across the state. "Talent is everywhere. Access is not" For Shradha Sharma, Founder and CEO of YourStory and Founder of The Bharat Project, ShuruKar marks a shift from documenting entrepreneurs to creating them. "For 17 years, I have told the stories of entrepreneurs. But somewhere along the way, I realised that telling their stories is not enough. We have to help create the next generation of them," she said. "Talent is everywhere in India. Ambition is everywhere. Access is not. ShuruKar is our attempt to change that." She had a direct message for anyone who has wanted to build something but stalled at the starting line: "To every young person who has ever thought, 'I want to do something of my own, but I don't know where to begin,' I want to say that you do not need to have all the answers. You just need to start." Sharma told the gathering that India's next generation of founders will come as much from Patna, Gaya, Darbhanga and Muzaffarpur as from the metros. ShuruKar, she said, will stay with them from finding the right problem to winning their first customer. A changing Bihar Minister Nitish Mishra spoke about the unseen side of every success story. "People see the success at the end of a journey, but they rarely see the struggle that went into it. Every entrepreneur faces that struggle, but let it not stop you," he said. He added that perceptions of the state are lagging behind reality. "Bihar is often seen in the wrong light, but the reality on the ground is changing. The government is doing a great deal to promote entrepreneurship and new businesses in the state, and young people should come forward and make full use of it." How ShuruKar works ShuruKar is a district-level platform that turns local problems into local enterprises. Every participant moves through four stages: Find the problem. The journey starts with identifying a real problem in the participant's own district. Shape the idea. Each participant gets an AI Copilot to refine the idea and plan the next step. Build with mentors. Experienced founders provide handholding and mentorship until the first customer is won. Tap local opportunity. The platform opens up district-level markets, networks and partners. ShuruKar is designed to work through existing government structures without creating a new scheme or seeking funding from the government. The launch also saw the announcement of the ShuruKar Challenge, which invites solutions to some of the country's most pressing problems. Inside the launch The day opened with addresses by the dignitaries and the formal launch of ShuruKar. Keynotes followed from Amar Dixit, CEO, WOI India, and Johnson Tellis, Co-Founder and CEO, InUnity. Founders then took the stage to share their journeys and answer questions from young people in the audience. Hokar Nidar, ShuruKar The event closed on the line that has come to define the movement: Hokar Nidar, ShuruKar. Do not just look for a job, learn how to create one. Do not wait for opportunity, start.

title: World Mental Health Day: Rest in the Age of AI
content: Some years ago, our attention span was 45 to 50 minutes. Today, it has reduced to just 47 seconds. There is a severe attention deficit today. The increased use of screens has a big role to play in this. When we stare at a screen for too long, we blink less. That affects the freshness and creativity of our minds. People today have more experiences than their senses and minds can handle. They feel emotionally exhausted and inwardly lost. The purpose of technology is to bring us comfort. If it becomes the cause of distress, its purpose is lost. Holding onto cell phones all day hurts the nervous system. But if you are free from stress, you will use technology for a good purpose. AI can have three interpretations. The first is the absence of intelligence. A lot of what comes on social media is fake and AI-driven. We have to move ahead in AI, but with awareness. We forget to recognise intelligence in nature, which is an absence of intelligence on our part. The second is artificial intelligence. It can only reproduce what is already stored, not create something new. It challenges our intellect and creativity, and pushes us to do something original. Do not see the advent of AI as a hindrance. When calculators entered schools, teachers feared students would lose the ability to calculate. That did not happen. The third meaning of AI is absolute intelligence. Wherever there is intelligence, there is consciousness. That one consciousness which envelops the whole universe is very orderly, and its intelligence is supreme. It connects us with a source deep within us which can bring out more creativity and enthusiasm. It can uplift the spirit around us and help us get over this terrible sense of loneliness. The root cause of loneliness is stress and disconnectedness from ourselves. When we become centred, when we settle deeply within ourselves, we naturally discover that we are a source of joy. Then, when people come together with a spirit of giving, serving, and contributing to each other's lives, genuine happiness follows. That is how loneliness is overcome, not by desperately searching for someone else, but by first becoming connected to ourselves. No machine can replicate real human connection. We convey more through presence, feeling, and vibration than just words. Technology can help, but it cannot improve one’s vibrations. If your vibrations are harmonious, positive, and joyful, everyone will love to be around you. Meditation makes your vibrations positive and makes you pleasant to be around. Meditation is not a luxury, but a basic need today. I call it mental hygiene, just like brushing is dental hygiene. Meditation is not about doing something, but about being. Like when you stop your car at the petrol pump, you turn it off so that you can fill it up. You can’t fill your car while driving. Once your car is full, you do not stay there; you drive. Similarly, we must pause to recharge ourselves, and then move back into activity with strength, clarity, and joy. The best ideas and solutions arise amidst deep silence and meditation. When you are rattled, even good ideas fail. Focus and presence of mind can come from rest, not from effort or activity. Technology must enable connection, wisdom, joy, and the journey within. When we move from the absence of intelligence to absolute intelligence, artificial intelligence finds its right place. By Gurudev Sri Sri Ravi Shankar

title: Nat Habit raises Rs 142 Cr in Series C led by Trident Growth Partners
content: Ayurvedic personal care brand Nat Habit has raised Rs 142 crore in a Series C funding round led by Trident Growth Partners. Existing investors Bertelsmann India Investments, Mirabilis Investment Trust and Sharrp Ventures also participated, alongside new investors Physis Capital and Hero Family Office. The company will use the fresh capital to expand its product portfolio, strengthen its formulation and manufacturing capabilities, and scale distribution across quick commerce platforms and offline retail channels. Founded in 2019 by Swagatika Das and Gaurav Agarwal, Nat Habit said its annualised gross revenue has reached Rs 330 crore. “ We started Nat Habit with a simple belief: natural personal care should never require consumers to compromise on freshness or efficacy. That belief has shaped our journey, from developing our formulations in-house, to building a brand that brings the goodness of Ayurveda into everyday personal care routines,” said Swagatika Das, Co-founder, Nat Habit. According to Nat Habit, the brand has built a differentiated proposition by combining traditional Ayurvedic principles with modern science to develop fresh formulations produced through in-house R&D and manufacturing capabilities. Its portfolio ranges across hair care, skin care, body care and baby care. Nat Habit is now aiming to go beyond the metro markets and makes its presence in Tier II and beyond markets. "India’s personal care market is evolving, with consumers increasingly seeking all-natural products they can trust for the whole family. Nat Habit has built a compelling business around Fresh Ayurveda, bringing natural goodness to everyday personal care through advanced in-house R&D, formulation and manufacturing,” said Atul Gupta, Managing Partner, Trident Growth Partners. Trident Growth Partners is a growth-stage private equity firm headquartered in Bengaluru, backing category-leading, founder-led businesses across consumer, financial services, enterprise technology, manufacturing and healthcare.

title: The festive sales playbook: How Amazon and Flipkart are winning India’s mega sales
content: If you’ve been tracking the annual showdown between Amazon’s Great Indian Festival and Flipkart’s Big Billion Days, it’s easy to get bogged down in the hype. Every year brings promises of bigger discounts and flashier launch events. But looking past the standard headlines this season, the actual narrative on the ground has shifted. The real battle isn't just about who knocks a few extra rupees off a television; it’s about instant fulfillment, structural supply chain pivots, and an aggressive push in Tier II and III cities. The Amazon Great Indian Festival started a day earlier on October 8 compared to Flipkart’s Big Billion Days. Flipkart started its sale on October 9, with early access to select members starting a day ahead. Preparing for the big sale days, Flipkart created 2.5 lakh new opportunities to support this year’s Big Billion Days. The biggest change in strategy this year comes down to delivery speed. Quick commerce has officially crossed over from grocery apps into mainstream ecommerce. Amazon brought its 10-to-15-minute quick delivery setup, Amazon Now, directly into its main festival sale for the first time. Supported by 800 micro-procurement centers in 120 cities, they were delivering flagship iPhones within minutes of the sale opening at midnight, on 8 October. Beyond the ultra-fast tier, Amazon opened up 10 million products for same-day delivery and another 40 million for next-day delivery nationwide. Flipkart has responded with a similar operational pivot, embedding Flipkart Minutes (internally known as Magenta) directly into its primary app. Rather than switching apps, shoppers can search once and choose quick delivery for fast-turnaround items. To keep up with the volume without breaking its logistics engine, Flipkart added 250,000 seasonal workers and expanded its Ekart network into 750 new pin codes. While metro cities drive significant transaction values, smaller urban centers are setting the pace for volume. Amazon hit 100% pin code coverage across India within hours of launch, with Tier-II and III cities generating 60% to 65% of total orders. Flipkart recorded nearly identical geographic demand, with over 60% of its order volume coming from non-metro markets. Digging into specific shopping categories reveals clear shifts in how consumers are spending their festive budgets. Mobile phones have shown surprising strength despite widespread industry talk about a cooling smartphone market. Amazon reported a 70% year-on-year jump in Android phone sales, driven by strong momentum from brands like Samsung, Xiaomi, and OnePlus, while premium flagship models across both platforms saw rapid initial uptake. Home upgrades are another major driver, with shoppers taking advantage of festive financing to upgrade core household electronics. Amazon said it logged a 90% year-on-year increase in large appliances like refrigerators, washing machines, and air conditioners, while overall TV sales doubled compared to last year. Within televisions, 55-inch models grew the fastest, showing a clear preference for larger screens and better display technology. Health and personal wellness products saw some of the most dramatic growth rates. On Amazon, wearable health trackers jumped 1,400% year-on-year, led by Apple, Samsung, and Whoop—which alone grew 900%. Air purifiers climbed 300% year-on-year, while premium treadmills also saw strong order volume. Niche lifestyle categories, specialty kitchenware, and gifting items posted notable numbers across both storefronts. Espresso machines, led by De'Longhi, grew 500% year-on-year on Amazon, while Korean beauty brands tripled their sales volume. Gifting-related categories saw dinnerware grow 500%, juicers rise 400%, Lego sets increase 212%, and handheld vacuums expand 200%. Over on Flipkart, high-volume unit orders in fashion, beauty, personal care, and home decor remained the backbone of daily order volume, driving up to 90% growth in non-metro regions. Flexible financing was a key driver in getting shoppers to complete these purchases. Amazon saw its no-cost EMI adoption rate jump from 30–35% last year to 50% in the opening hours of this sale, meaning one out of every two eligible purchases used structured financing. Flipkart reported a 30% to 40% rise in no-cost EMI usage, with customers increasingly applying credit to lower-ticket items like fashion rather than keeping it strictly for high-end electronics. Finally, both platforms leaned on tech and media to help shoppers navigate their massive catalogs. Amazon deployed its AI shopping assistant, Rufus, to handle millions of customer queries in English and regional languages—helping with product comparisons, deal discovery, and installation details. Flipkart focused heavily on creator-led social commerce, mobilising an ecosystem of 200,000 monthly creators on platforms like Meta to run targeted video content aimed at Gen Z and younger shoppers, who now account for nearly 40% of its customer base."

title: [Weekly funding roundup Oct 3-9] Steep decline in VC inflow
content: Venture capital funding into Indian startups recorded a sharp decline and this was largely due to the absence of large deals during this week. The total funding this week came in at $168 million across 28 deals. In comparison, the previous week saw a total amount raised at $418 million. Last week, there were two deals with value above $100 million but this week, the highest funded deal was of TVS Automotive Solutions at $44 million. This shows the uncertain nature of VC funding into the Indian startup ecosystem in the current environment as there are no definite trends that define the capital inflow. In addition, when investors are focused on the artificial intelligence segment, there is no credible story from India as yet. This also explains the lower funding volume into the ecosystem. Interestingly, this week there were a few deals which were focused on the consumer tech segment. These are ventures which have created distinct brands in a highly competitive market. Key transactions TVS Automobile Solutions owned myTVS raised Rs 425 crore ($44 million approx.) led by CE-Invests. Lifestyle brand DailyObjects raised Rs 332 crore ($34.3 million approx.) from Xponentia Capital Partners, Anicut Capital, and Axiom Asia Private Capital. Consumer tech brand Lumio raised $12 million from Blume Ventures, Stellaris Venture Partners and 3one4 Capital. Kitchen appliances brand Beyond Appliances raised Rs 110 crore ($11.3 million approx.) from Fireside Ventures, Dharana Capital and others. Deeptech startup Quanfluence raised $10 million from Chiratae Ventures, Pi Ventures and Rainmatter by Zerodha. Edtech company byteXL raised $9 million from Elevar Equity, Kalaari Capital, and The Michael & Susan Dell Foundation. MSME-focused digital lender NeoGrowth raised Rs 85 crore ($8.8 million approx.) from FMO and LeapFrog Investments. Medtech company Sunfox Technologies raised $7 million from Ashish Kacholia, Lashit Sanghvi, Alchemy Capital and 3one4 Capital. Deeptech startup QpiAI raised Rs 50 crore ($5.1 million) from InnoVen Capital India Fund II.

title: Startup news and updates: daily roundup (October 9, 2026)
content: YourStory presents the daily news roundup from the Indian startup ecosystem and beyond. Here's the roundup for Thursday, October 8 , 2026. Funding news NeoGrowth raises Rs 85 crore led by FMO MSME-focused digital lender NeoGrowth has raised Rs 85 crore in an investment round led by FMO, the Dutch entrepreneurial development bank, with participation from existing investor LeapFrog Investments. The funding will support the company's next growth phase, including expanding access to credit for micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), strengthening its digital lending capabilities, and deepening its market presence. Read more Other news EyeROV delivers two indigenous underwater robotic systems to Indian Navy Kochi-based marine robotics company EyeROV has delivered two TROUT military-grade remotely operated underwater vehicles to the Indian Navy. The delivery forms part of an order for five systems and marks progress in India’s development of indigenous underwater robotic technology. Developed under the Innovations for Defence Excellence (iDEX) programme, TROUT is designed for naval and subsea operations, including underwater inspection, surveillance, reconnaissance, search and recovery, and robotic intervention. The system underwent field trials and qualification processes covering manoeuvrability, navigation, endurance and performance in challenging underwater conditions. It also completed type testing and quality assurance procedures aligned with applicable military standards. Accenture and Dell expand partnership to scale enterprise AI Accenture and Dell Technologies have expanded their more than 20-year collaboration by establishing the Accenture Dell Business Group. The initiative aims to help enterprises modernise infrastructure and deploy AI at scale, with greater control over data, costs, and performance. The collaboration will focus on private AI infrastructure, hybrid and sovereign environments, agentic AI applications and integrated enterprise AI solutions. It will also support organisations operating in highly regulated industries that require stronger control over sensitive information. BuyBuyCart launches B2B wholesale ordering platform Retail supermarket chain BuyBuyCart has launched a business-to-business platform designed to streamline wholesale operations and digital ordering across its franchise network. The platform is being developed as a centralised system for wholesale and franchise orders. Its features include state-wise order tracking, value- and quantity-based analysis, franchise-wise ordering, salesperson performance monitoring and product-level sales insights. As the platform evolves, the company plans to enable franchise partners to place routine and replenishment orders directly through the portal. JSW MG Motor India selects eight startups for MG Developer Program JSW MG Motor India has selected eight startups as winners of the sixth edition of its MG Developer Program, an initiative supporting innovation in mobility and emerging technologies. The selected companies are Nayan Technologies, Technod8.AI, LiveNSense, LW3, Smaartbrand by Acquink Solutions, Fitsol, Cautio and Meta Materials Circular Market. Their solutions cover road intelligence, agentic AI, industrial intelligence, electric-vehicle battery supply-chain compliance, customer decision intelligence, supply-chain decarbonisation, mobility intelligence, and automotive circular-economy infrastructure. The winners will work with JSW MG Motor India and its partners to explore pilot projects and real-world deployments. Zomato and Blinkit’s EV Bazaar attracts 2,500 delivery partners Eternal’s Zomato and Blinkit have hosted the third edition of EV Bazaar in New Delhi to encourage electric vehicle adoption among delivery partners. The event attracted 2,500 delivery partners and ecosystem participants, including more than 20 electric vehicle manufacturers, which showcased over 30 electric two-wheeler models. The initiative enables delivery partners to compare vehicles, explore rental and ownership options, and understand charging and battery-swapping facilities. Four India-linked startups feature in Y Combinator cohorts Four startups founded by alumni of Indian educational institutions are developing AI-driven solutions across hardware procurement, enterprise software, pharmaceutical documentation and video editing. The document features Waybill, Ressl AI, Ritivel, and Cardboard. Waybill, founded by Plaksha University alumni Rishi Laddha and Tushar Goyal, aims to simplify hardware procurement by combining supplier discovery, ordering, payments, shipping, customs and inventory management. Ressl AI, founded by IIT Bombay alumni Arushi Gandhi and Abhishek Eswaran, uses AI agents to automate repetitive maintenance tasks in enterprise software. Ritivel, founded by IIT Bombay alumni Pavan Kalyan Tankala, Nirmit Arora and Gunin Gupta, develops AI tools to draft pharmaceutical regulatory documents while linking information to its sources. Cardboard, founded by BITS Pilani alumni Saksham Aggarwal and Ishan Sharma, is building a browser-based AI video editor that converts raw footage into initial cuts using natural-language instructions. Aditya Birla World Academy hosts student-led mental health festival Aditya Birla World Academy hosted The Happy Place, a student-led mental health festival supported by Mpower, bringing students together to explore emotional well-being through creative expression. The latest edition, themed ‘The Messy Middle’, focused on uncertainty, setbacks and self-doubt experienced during adolescence. The school said it integrates mental health education into its curriculum through Minds Matter, which covers students in Grades 1 to 12. The initiative aims to encourage open conversations about emotions, develop coping strategies and help students seek support when needed. Harness acquires select Augment Code assets Harness has acquired select assets from Augment Code, including Cosmos, the Auggie CLI products, the Code Context Engine and related technology. The acquisition aims to accelerate Harness’s efforts to automate software development across the software delivery lifecycle. Cosmos will become the Harness Cosmos Software Factory Agent, designed to turn requirements, tickets and bug reports into code and tests before opening pull requests for review. The system uses AI agents to plan changes, write code and address reviewer feedback, with engineers involved where human judgement is required. Harness plans to combine Augment’s codebase understanding capabilities with its Software Delivery Knowledge Graph, which provides information about builds, deployments, security and operational costs. Cummins India appoints Gbile Adewunmi as managing director Cummins India has appointed Gbile Adewunmi as Managing Director of Cummins India Limited and India Regional Leader, effective November 1, 2026. He will take on the expanded responsibilities alongside his current role leading Industrial Markets within the company’s Power Systems business. Adewunmi currently serves as Vice President of Power Systems Industrial Markets, working with customers and partners across industrial sectors, including mining. Kore.ai launches Autoloop for continuous AI agent optimisation Kore.ai has announced the general availability of Autoloop, an optimisation engine within its Agent Platform, Artemis edition. The capability is designed to build, evaluate and continuously improve enterprise AI agents against business-defined goals, reducing reliance on manual adjustments. Autoloop assesses agents across task completion, accuracy, adherence to business rules, safety, consistency, user experience and cost efficiency. Its continuous process covers building, evaluation, diagnosis, optimisation and verification, both before deployment and during production. Atlassian unveils new AI collaboration capabilities Atlassian has announced new AI collaboration capabilities at its Team ’26 Europe conference in Amsterdam, including the Agentic Multiplayer Protocol (AMP). The framework establishes guidelines for AI agents to work alongside human teams across digital tools and workflows. AMP covers collaboration within existing work environments, clear agent identities and ownership, and governance controls governing access to organisational information. It also supports auditability, permissions and human checkpoints for important decisions. Atlassian said people and agents collaborate more than 10 million times each month across its platform, while the number of Rovo agent users has doubled in six months. Scalefusion launches vulnerability management capability Scalefusion has launched Veltar Vulnerability Management, a capability that connects vulnerability detection with remediation through its unified endpoint management platform. The offering enables IT and security teams to identify vulnerabilities across managed Windows and macOS devices, assess risks and deploy fixes through existing patch management workflows. The system combines vulnerability severity, threat intelligence and endpoint information to help organisations prioritise remediation. Its signals include the Common Vulnerability Scoring System, Exploit Prediction Scoring System, CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities data and Device Risk Score. Spardha School of Music launches technology-enabled training platform Spardha School of Music has expanded its digital learning ecosystem with a training platform designed to support music and performing arts students beyond scheduled classes. The platform combines one-to-one teaching with practice tools, assignments, progress tracking and AI-powered feedback. Students can access practice videos and sheet music and use tools such as metronomes, virtual keyboards, tabla, mridangam and tanpura. AI-powered session notes, monthly progress reports, and real-time practice feedback help learners track their progress. The platform also supports teacher performance monitoring and personalised professional development. Mirror Security selected for Google for Startups cybersecurity programme Mirror Security has been selected for the inaugural Google for Startups Gemini Startup Forum: Cybersecurity, joining 33 cybersecurity startups chosen globally. The company participated in the programme at Google’s London office on September 8 and 9, 2026, where founders engaged with experts from Google Cloud and Google DeepMind. The company was selected under the AI Security and Governance category for its use of fully homomorphic encryption, which allows data to remain encrypted while AI models process it. Its technology aims to protect sensitive information contained in prompts, embeddings and agent messages as organisations deploy AI applications. New Relic introduces AI evaluation capabilities New Relic has announced AI Evaluation, a new capability within its AI Observability offering designed to assess generative AI performance across the application lifecycle. The platform evaluates response quality, behaviour, security risks and business impact, extending visibility beyond individual large language model interactions. The capability uses automated evaluations to identify issues such as hallucinations, prompt injections, data leaks, toxicity and bias. It connects quality scores with application traces, helping engineering teams investigate problems across prompts, retrieval systems and backend infrastructure. Rocket Learning convenes policymakers and experts at Udaan 2026 Rocket Learning hosted Udaan 2026 in New Delhi, bringing together policymakers, researchers, educators, civil society representatives and technology leaders to discuss early childhood care and education. The event, themed ‘From Surviving to Thriving’, focused on strengthening Anganwadis, increasing investment in early childhood development and using technology to support young children. The conference also presented findings from an evaluation of a technology-based early childhood development model, examining its impact and cost-effectiveness. NWWA and Mpower launch mental health initiative for NDRF families The NDRF Wives Welfare Association (NWWA) has signed a memorandum of understanding with Mpower to launch Project Nirmal, a mental health and psychosocial support initiative for National Disaster Response Force personnel and their families. The programme aims to address occupational stress associated with disaster response, demanding working conditions and sudden deployments. Services will include mental health awareness sessions, psychological screening, individual and group counselling, tele-counselling, crisis intervention and suicide prevention support. The initiative will also establish regional teams and operate a dedicated multilingual helpline round the clock. Varun Dhawan invests in biofortified staples brand Better Nutrition Actor Varun Dhawan has joined Better Nutrition, a biofortified staples brand featured on Shark Tank India, as an investor and brand ambassador. His association with the company began with his own farming journey, which sparked an interest in soil, seeds and nutrient-rich food. He joins existing brand ambassador PV Sindhu as Better Nutrition looks to expand awareness of biofortified food among Indian consumers. Better Nutrition offers everyday staples, including atta, dal, rice and millets, made from crops developed to contain higher levels of essential micronutrients such as iron and zinc. The company uses biofortified seeds, soil science and farm-level testing, including X-ray fluorescence technology, to measure nutrient levels. As part of the association, Dhawan's farm will also be developed as a biofortified farm in partnership with the company. Vivriti Asset Management returns over Rs 3,400 Cr to investors Vivriti Asset Management (VAM) has completed the lifecycle and exit of its Vintage II funds within the stipulated period, returning more than Rs 3,400 crore to investors through capital repayments and income distributions across two fund vintages. The Vintage II funds raised Rs 1,700 crore in investor commitments and invested over Rs 3,500 crore across more than 45 portfolio companies. Their investments spanned infrastructure, clean energy, manufacturing, logistics and enterprise software. The funds collectively returned over Rs 2,260 crore in capital and income. The moderate-risk scheme generated a gross internal rate of return (IRR) of approximately 15%, while the conservative scheme delivered around 12%. Net returns were approximately 13% and 10.5%, respectively. VAM has invested over Rs 12,500 crore across 125-plus portfolio companies since inception. Mi Arcus partners Papa Don't Preach for festive kidswear Kidswear brand Mi Arcus has partnered with designer label Papa Don't Preach to launch a premium festive collection for children on October 12. The collection will be available through Mi Arcus stores, its website and e-commerce platforms, including Nykaa Fashion and Myntra. The collaboration marks Papa Don't Preach’s first partnership with a kidswear brand and Mi Arcus’s entry into ethnic wear. The collection combines playful designs and bold colours with soft fabrics and comfortable silhouettes. BUSY Infotech targets Rs 1,000 crore revenue in five years BUSY Infotech, a subsidiary of IndiaMART, is targeting revenue of approximately Rs 1,000 crore over the next five years, aiming for five- to sixfold growth as Indian MSMEs increasingly adopt digital business management tools. The accounting and GST compliance software provider reported revenue of Rs 170 crore in FY26. Its revenue from operations rose around 47% year-on-year to Rs 36 crore in Q1 FY27, while cash from operations more than doubled to Rs 44 crore in FY26 from Rs 21 crore in FY25. More than six lakh companies use BUSY software. The company plans to accelerate customer acquisition, expand cloud and mobile offerings, introduce AI-powered features and strengthen its presence in western, southern and eastern India. It will also explore strategic acquisitions to expand its products and market reach.

title: Orkut creator seeks to revive the iconic social network platform
content: Orkut Büyükkökten, the creator of orkut.com, is seeking to revive the platform, which introduced many people to social networking. “The internet should help us find our people. Friendship. Community. A place to belong,” Büyükkökten wrote on X, adding, “Help me bring Orkut back in that spirit.” Büyükkökten has created four social networking platforms , the most recent of which was Hello.com. He is now hoping to revive Orkut. The entrepreneur has invited people to add their names to the Orkut website, effectively signing a petition calling for a new social network “focused on authentic people, real connection, and genuine belonging.” As of October 9, the website had received more than 2,70,000 signatures, most of them from Brazil. Portugal, Ireland and Paraguay were among the other countries represented. Also Read The untold story of Orkut Büyükkökten—the man who built world’s largest social network before Mark Zuckerberg Büyükkökten created Orkut as a side project while working at Google. The social network was launched in January 2004, about two weeks before Facebook's launch. Orkut was owned and operated by Google until its closure in September 2014. In 2008, Büyükkökten left the Orkut team to take up a product manager role at Google. By this time, Facebook was expanding internationally, refining its design, privacy controls, and third-party application ecosystem. Orkut, meanwhile, grew to more than 300 million users worldwide and became a defining part of internet culture in Brazil, India and beyond. However, Facebook overtook Orkut in India in July 2010 and Brazil in December 2011, according to Comscore audience data. Despite its strong following in India and Brazil, Orkut did not achieve comparable popularity in many Western markets, while Facebook continued to expand globally. It also faced notable security incidents, including a worm that exploited its Scrapbook feature in 2007. Meanwhile, Google launched Google+, a social networking and identity service, in June 2011. On June 30, 2014, Google announced that it would close Orkut on September 30, 2014, explaining that YouTube, Blogger and Google+ had grown faster. The decision reflected the company's decision to shift resources towards its other social platforms. Edited by Swetha Kannan

title: Few H-1B workers transitioning to green cards via PERM: Nasscom
content: Indian IT industry body Nasscom highlighted that few employees transition from H-1B visas to permanent residency through the Permanent Labor Certification (PERM) process. This response comes in the wake of the US government's announcement that it will not take any new PERM applications from Indian technology companies including TCS, Infosys, Wipro, and HCLTech. “Indian technology companies operate across more than 80 countries and have consistently demonstrated their commitment to complying with local laws and regulatory requirements. We are confident that they will continue to adhere to applicable regulations in the US as well,” a statement from Nasscom said. Indian IT companies have historically been the largest recipients of H-1B visas and have come under attack from successive governments for supposedly displacing US citizens from work opportunities. Nasscom pointed that Indian technology companies have significantly reduced their dependence on H-1B visas, while steadily expanding local hiring and building a strong domestic workforce in the U.S. It also added that Indian IT companies are closely engaged with Fortune 500 corporations to drive their innovation agenda. "The number of employees transitioning from H-1B visas to permanent residency through the PERM process is also relatively limited," the body said. Nasscom has consistently maintained that immigration and skilled talent mobility are two distinct issues and should not be viewed through the same lens. H-1B visas is a six year work visas which is used to address the skill shortage gap in the US TCS said its PERM applications were in single digits in the last two years and does not expect suspension of the programm to impact its workforce strategy and customer engagements. The company said it intends to hire 15,000 people in the US over the next five years and added that its has built a significant local workforce across 31 offices and delivery centers throughout the country. The $300 billion plus Indian IT industry generates around 60% of its revenues from the US market and policy change has a bearing on the sector. Gaurav Vasu, CEO and Founder, UnearthInsight said the US suspension of the PERM programme will pressure IT services margins before it meaningfully affects revenue. “Our estimates suggest negligible immediate revenue impact, but 10–30 basis points of operating-margin pressure over the next 12 months, primarily due to the need to retain experienced US-based staff and hire replacements. If the suspension persists for several years, margin pressure could rise to 30–75 basis points, with revenues coming in 0.25–0.75% below otherwise expected levels,” he noted. Besides the Indian IT companies, others like Microsoft, Adobe, Capgemini came under scrutiny for their PERM progamme. “Since 2009, these companies alone have requested almost three million foreign workers. They've received over 230,000 H-1B visa approvals and more than 100,000 permanent labour certifications,” Keith Sonderling, US Labour Secretary said. Indian-American lawmaker, Pramila Jayapal slammed the Trump administration’s decision to suspend the Green Card pathway for Microsoft, saying the move undermines legal immigration and weakens America’s ability to innovate. (With additional inputs from PTI)

title: NABARD-backed NABVENTURES raises Rs 450 Cr for second fund
content: NABVENTURES, the venture capital arm of the National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD), has achieved the first close of its second fund, securing Rs 450 crore in initial commitments. The fund has a target corpus of Rs 1,500 crore, including a green-shoe option to accommodate additional investments. NABARD is the anchor investor in the fund, which will back early- to growth-stage technology startups focused on agriculture and rural development. Established on April 23, 2018, as a wholly owned subsidiary of NABARD, NABVENTURES manages investments through its flagship Fund I and the specialised AgriSURE fund. The firm has invested in 23 companies across India's agritech and rural startup ecosystem. Its portfolio includes supply chain platform Unnati, farm-to-consumer brand Eggoz, snacking company Beyond Snack, and rural fintech startup Jai Kisan. Earlier this year, aquaculture-focused agritech startup Aquapulse raised Rs 25 crore in an ongoing Series A round led by NABVENTURES and KisaanSay, with the investment made through the AgriSURE fund. NABVENTURES Fund II will provide growth capital to companies using technology to address structural challenges across the agricultural value chain. Its focus areas include agritech, climate-smart solutions, supply chain and logistics, rural fintech, food and agribusiness, and other businesses driving rural transformation. Announcing the First Close, Dr. Shaji Krishnan V, Chairman of NABARD stated, "The successful First Close of NABVENTURES Fund II at Rs 450 crore marks an important milestone in NABARD's continued commitment to fostering innovation across India's agriculture and rural economy. As the sector evolves, there is a growing need for scalable, technology-driven solutions that enhance productivity, strengthen value chains, improve farmers' incomes, and build resilient rural enterprises.” “Through Fund II, we aim to partner with visionary entrepreneurs developing innovative solutions to address critical challenges across the agricultural ecosystem. Our focus is on supporting enterprises that deliver both strong commercial outcomes and meaningful social impact through sustainability, climate resilience, financial inclusion, and livelihood creation. By deepening support for the innovation ecosystem, NABARD seeks to accelerate the transformation of India's agriculture and rural economy, making it more resilient, competitive, and future-ready,” he added. The deployment of fresh capital comes during an extended funding recalibration within India's agritech sector. Startups in the sector raised $202 million across 36 deals in 2025, reflecting a 25% decline from the $269 million recorded in 2024. The recent pullback contrasts sharply with the sector's peak investment activity in 2021 and 2022, when funding reached $728 million and $840 million, respectively. Market analysts attribute the slowdown to heightened investor scrutiny over capital-intensive operations, elevated customer acquisition costs, and monetization challenges among marketplace and logistics platforms. The wider Indian venture ecosystem has reflected similar cautious sentiment. In the third quarter of 2026, total startup funding rose 5% year-over-year to $2.2 billion, even as deal volume fell 13% and the active investor pool contracted 24%. Despite broader headwinds, established agritech operations continue to secure target capital. Farm machinery developer Balwaan Krishi raised $10.4 million in a Series B round in September, while B2B agri-supply chain platform Ninjacart secured $6 million in July. NABVENTURES' Rs 1,500 crore fund target signals institutional confidence in the long-term commercial potential of India's rural economy.""

title: Juspay FY26 revenue rises 30% to Rs 664 Cr as international business and AI bets scale
content: Payments technology company Juspay reported a 30% year-on-year increase in revenue for the financial year ended March 31, 2026 (FY26), reaching Rs 664 crore, up from Rs 514 crore in FY25. The top-line growth reflects sustained momentum across the company's core operations, with revenue more than tripling over a three-year period from Rs 213 crore in FY23, representing a compound annual growth rate of approximately 46%. The Bengaluru-headquartered fintech firm remained Adjusted EBITDA positive at Rs 33 crore for FY26, excluding non-cash ESOP costs. However, increased capital allocation towards global market expansion and deep-tech artificial intelligence infrastructure widened its net loss to Rs 90 crore for the fiscal year. Juspay’s platform scaled to process 400 million daily transactions during the year, driving an annualised Total Payment Volume past the $1 trillion milestone with a reported 99.999% uptime reliability. The platform currently powers payment orchestration for more than 500 enterprises and financial institutions globally, including Amazon, Swiggy, Flipkart, Google, IndiGo, Agoda, HSBC, IKEA, and Zurich Insurance. During FY26, Juspay accelerated its international footprint across North America, Europe, Latin America, the Middle East, and the Asia-Pacific region, alongside continuous scaling and profitability within its domestic Indian payments division. A substantial portion of the capital deployed throughout the year was directed into developing proprietary, open-source AI infrastructure tailored for enterprise workflows and agentic commerce. Key technological platforms developed during the period include Xyne, an open-source, model-agnostic, and data-sovereign enterprise AI framework built on Unix-like architecture. The firm also rolled out Juspay Genius, an AI-native payment intelligence suite designed to automate enterprise payment management, routing logic, and analytics. Additional launches included Breeze Buddy, a no-code AI voice platform supporting automated customer support, and Breeze Universal, which facilitates brand discovery across third-party AI ecosystems. Commenting on the financial performance, Sheetal Lalwani, Co-founder and Chief Operating Officer at Juspay, stated that FY26 marked a pivotal investment period geared towards laying infrastructure for the company’s next phase of global growth. "FY26 was a year of investing in the capabilities that will support Juspay’s next phase of growth. Our international payments business is scaling, and we are beginning to see traction across markets. As we expand globally, we are also investing in AI as part of a broader strategy to build new solutions for enterprises," Lalwani said. "Xyne is one example of this investment, bringing our experience in building reliable, enterprise-grade infrastructure to an open-source AI platform." Lalwani acknowledged the short-term impact of these capital deployments on near-term net earnings, noting that the strategy remains anchored in building long-term capabilities, expanding technical talent, and establishing sustainable value for enterprise clients. Founded in 2012, Juspay currently operates with a global workforce of over 1,500 employees across key international hubs including Bengaluru, San Francisco, Dublin, São Paulo, Singapore, and Dubai.""

title: The next chapter for India’s insurtech is about reach, trust, and retention
content: During calendar year (CY) 2025, Insurtech IPOs and acquisitions hit multi-year highs, even as fresh venture funding into the category grew at a slower rate. Investors are showing more interest in insurance technology but also asking harder questions from companies showing commercial traction. Insurtech, the sector that uses modern technology to make traditional insurance products and processes faster, cheaper, and more personal, is on a rally. India’s insurtech sector is one of the largest in the world, and its choices will shape the next decade of insurance distribution here. According to an October 2025 report by BCG and India InsurTech Association (IIA), India’s insurtech ecosystem has over 150 active players, with cumulative valuations crossing $15.8 billion and revenue reaching $0.9 billion in 2024, a tenfold increase since 2019. The sector has two unicorns, eight players between $100 million and $1 billion and over 45 players with over $1 million. India’s insurtech sector mirrored the global trends, signalling a shift in investor focus to backing businesses with clear paths to profitability and scale, according to the report. Health Insurtech ventures in India accounted for four of the five largest deals and more than 70% of the funding, reflecting their role in driving access, efficiency, and innovation. For much of the past decade, the sector was aiming for scale. This got global capital excited about a market where insurance penetration has been stuck near 3.7% of GDP for years, roughly half the world average. However, the excitement about India’s large addressable market is also a tale of caution, as many insurance distribution companies have had to raise funds regularly to survive. Insurance is difficult to scale responsibly, and the reasons have less to do with technology than with the product itself. For instance, a ride-hailing trip or a food-ordering app proves out its unit economics within days. However, an insurance policy plays out over a year, or five years, or sometimes a lifetime. So, insurtech start-ups cannot simply borrow growth playbooks built for other consumer internet businesses. The sheer cost of distribution in a country where insurance, outside a few urban pockets, is underpenetrated and where regulation is focused more on solvency, claim settlement and disclosure than growth rates, requires an approach that rewards patience over speed. The question, therefore, is what sustainable insurtech looks like amid the challenges the sector faces. To be sure, for years, presence across a large share of India's pincodes was the metric most insurance firms were chasing. It mattered far less whether that customer later bought a different product from the same platform. However, the mindset is slowly changing, with renewal rates and cross-selling turning customer acquisition costs into investments. For instance, an insurance advisor in a small town might spend a Tuesday following up on a claim filed three months earlier, and walking a family through why a certain hospital expense was covered and another was not. That conversation, far more than any app notification or online offers, is what brings the family back when the renewal falls due, and it is often what brings a neighbour or an extended family member to the same advisor looking for a policy of their own. A second shift is toward hybrid distribution, human advisors backed by digital tools, rather than the app-only acquisition approach. The advisor becomes both the acquisition engine and the retention engine, when trust is built through conversation rather than online. That same advisor also chases down missing documents, explaining a rejected claim, or simply answering a call when a policyholder does not know who else to ask. It is this servicing layer, built one interaction at a time, that turns a policy sold into a relationship kept, adding service as its own point, next to Trust and Access, the key pillars of the business. A third, still-emerging shift is that across India's broader insurance sector, from large life insurers to smaller distribution platforms, growth is increasingly being built organically by addressing the expanding population. However, some companies are also expanding inorganically, especially through mergers, acquisitions and foreign investments in order to scale quickly to meet the growing demand. In its early 2026 report on the Indian insurance market, Swiss Re Ltd, a Swiss reinsurance company, predicted the country’s mid-term annual premium growth at 6.9% annually between 2026 and 2030, making India the strongest growing major insurance market globally. Even for the insurtech sector, acquiring an existing agent network or customer base can help in scaling up quickly to tap the market. Perhaps this is the reason why the central government had once considered merging the loss-making state-owned insurers. The centre has since then asked these companies to focus on profitability, with the government monitoring their performance for a possible decision in the future. To be sure, even policy has started nudging the sector towards consolidation. The opening of 100% foreign direct investment into insurance, the recent rationalisation of GST on individual life and health premiums, and the regulator's own emphasis on capital efficiency and faster claim settlements point towards a sector that wants to be judged on outcomes for policyholders and not headlines about funding raised. However, none of this means growth stops mattering, as India remains badly under-insured, and closing that gap needs both existing and new players to push harder. Domestic rating agency, ICRA Ltd., in its April 2026 report on the Indian insurance sector, said it expects the individual New Business Premium (NBP) to rise by 9.4-9.9% to Rs 2.02-2.03 trillion in FY 2027, driven by private insurers. NBP is the total money collected from newly sold insurance policies industry wide. The rating agency expects overall NBP to rise by 7.8-8.2% to Rs 4.95-4.97 trillion in FY2027 from Rs 4.60 trillion in FY 2026 and Rs 3.97 trillion in FY 2025. Having spent close to a decade building an insurance distribution business from a handful of towns into a nationwide network, we believe the insurtech companies that matter five years from now will be the ones that create real value for this growing ecosystem, while also treating every funding round as a fuel for growing the business. title: Beyond Appliances raises Rs 110 Cr in Series B round led by Fireside Ventures
content: Kitchen appliances brand Beyond Appliances has raised Rs 110 crore in a Series B round of funding led by Fireside Ventures, with participation from Dharana Capital and other investors. The Bengaluru-based company will use the funding towards research and development and its new manufacturing plant. The startup will also use the capital to enter new product categories in the kitchen appliances space and strengthen its presence across its existing portfolio. Beyond Appliances' co-founder & CEO Eshwar K Vikas said, “We believe the next big shift in the appliance industry will come from building products that are not only technologically advanced but are fundamentally designed around how Indian households cook and live. The opportunity ahead is significantly larger, and this investment gives us the ability to pursue it with greater ambition.” Founded in 2024 by Eshwar K Vikas and Rakesh Patil, Beyond Appliances follows an omnichannel strategy with a retail presence in Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru and Hyderabad and a manufacturing facility is in Bengaluru. Its range of products include Android chimneys, Plug-N-Play chimneys, smart hobs, and cooktops. Beyond Appliances plans to expand its offline presence to 10 more cities over the next three years. The company says 15% of its revenue comes through customer referrals. Rakesh Patil, Co-Founder & CTO, Beyond Appliances, said, “Over the last two years, our R&D teams have worked closely with consumers to identify everyday challenges in Indian kitchens and translate those insights into products that are genuinely different.” Shuchi Pandya, Principal, Fireside Ventures, said, “ Very few early-stage brands demonstrate the depth of fundamentals that Beyond Appliances has built at this stage of its journey. From technology-led products and a growing omnichannel presence to strong in-house R&D and manufacturing capabilities, the company has taken a thoughtful approach to building a differentiated consumer brand.”

title: Why finance teams need to think in systems
content: Finance has always had a role beyond recording transactions. It is involved in planning, controls, treasury, risk, and decision-making. What is changing is the extent to which finance teams are also involved in the systems through which financial activity takes place. A customer's payment information can now move through a website or app, a payment system, an invoicing platform, a bank account, and an accounting system before it appears in a financial report. If those systems do not communicate, someone has to fill the gaps: checking transactions, moving data, downloading reports, and matching records manually. As businesses grow, it becomes harder to manage. Finance teams are becoming more involved in how these processes are designed. They are looking at where data comes from, where it needs to go, which steps can be automated, and how different systems should work together. Finance remains responsible for financial control, visibility, and decision-making. But fulfilling that responsibility increasingly requires an understanding of the systems behind the numbers. From recording transactions to designing workflows Consider a typical payment. A customer pays an invoice online. The payment needs to be recorded, the invoice updated, the money sent to the right bank account, and the transaction eventually reconciled with the accounting records. When each step sits in a different system, finance teams can end up doing much of this work manually. The same applies as businesses add subscriptions, recurring payments, payment links, marketplaces, or physical locations. Finance may also have to manage refunds, disputes, settlements, payouts, and multiple banking relationships. So payments are becoming part of a wider financial workflow, not a series of individual transactions. Technology can take some of the repetitive work out of this process. More importantly, it lets finance teams look at the workflow as a whole. Can a successful payment automatically update an invoice? Can payment information move into accounting without being entered again? Can a failed transaction trigger the next step without someone having to monitor it? These are questions about how financial processes should work, and technology can help make them happen. Finance starts thinking in systems Accounting and financial controls remain at the centre of the function, but finance professionals also need to be comfortable with data, digital systems, and the way information moves between them. A 2025 Wolters Kluwer survey of 100 senior finance executives in India found that 74% ranked digital transformation as a top priority, while 66% prioritized workflow automation. The survey also identified fragmented systems and data silos as challenges for finance teams. Finance professionals do not need to become software developers. But they do need to understand what a system can do, where a process is breaking down, and what should happen when two systems need to exchange information. As routine work becomes more automated, finance teams can spend more time on analysis, planning, problem-solving, and working with other parts of the business. That also brings them closer to decisions about how processes are built, how different systems connect, and where technology can improve them. Also Read When payments grow beyond the gateway Connecting financial systems An API allows different software applications to exchange information and interact with each other. For finance teams, this means that payment information related to payments does not have to stop at the payment platform. Transaction information can move into systems handling invoices, accounting, orders, or customer records. For example, once a customer completes a payment, that transaction information can pass to another application, which can update the relevant financial record or trigger the next step in the workflow. Zoho Payments provides REST-based APIs that allow businesses to incorporate payment functionality into their applications. It also supports webhooks, which can send real-time notifications when events such as successful or failed payments, refunds, and payouts take place. For finance, the value is in what these connections let the business do. Payment collection, invoicing, and reconciliation can become one workflow, instead of separate activities that require moving information between systems. Building finance operations that can scale A process that works when a business handles a few dozen transactions can become a bottleneck as the number of customers, invoices, payment methods, and bank transactions grows. More manual work also creates more opportunities for errors and mismatches. Connected systems can help businesses handle more volume without increasing manual work at the same rate. They can reduce the need to move information between systems manually, limit mismatches, and give finance teams better visibility into financial activity. Zoho Payments is one example of this connected approach.When used with Zoho Books, payment information can flow into the accounting workflow, helping businesses record collections, track settlements, and reconcile transactions. For businesses with more specific requirements, APIs provide another way to connect payment functionality with existing applications and workflows. The aim is to make payments, invoices, and reconciliation work together rather than treating them as separate tasks. This can give finance teams more control over how financial information moves through the business, while reducing the amount of manual intervention as transaction volumes grow. The finance team will still close the books, manage cash, and oversee reporting. But it is also likely to have a greater role in deciding which systems connect, which tasks should be automated, and how financial data moves from one part of the business to another. Finance isn’t becoming IT. But understanding the numbers increasingly means understanding the systems that move them.

title: 7 Books that teach you how to think under pressure
content: Pressure is an unavoidable part of life. Whether it arrives as a looming deadline, a difficult decision, a personal setback, or an unexpected crisis, the ability to think clearly under stress often determines how well we respond. While pressure can cloud judgment and trigger emotional reactions, it can also become an opportunity to develop resilience, focus, and confidence. The good news is that clear thinking under pressure is not simply an inborn trait. It is a skill that can be learned and strengthened over time. Some of the best insights on decision-making, mental toughness, emotional control, and resilience can be found in books that explore how people navigate challenging situations. Here are seven books that can help you stay calm, think clearly, and make better decisions when the stakes are high. 1. The Comfort Crisis by Michael Easter Modern life often shields us from discomfort, but growth happens when we learn to face challenges. Easter explores how embracing controlled hardship can build resilience, confidence, and the ability to stay calm under pressure. 2. The Art of Clear Thinking by Hasard Lee Written by a former U.S. Air Force fighter pilot, this book examines how people can make better decisions in high-stakes situations. Lee shares practical strategies for reducing panic, evaluating risks, and thinking clearly when every second counts. 3. Building a Second Brain by Tiago Forte Pressure often comes from information overload. Forte's book teaches readers how to organise knowledge effectively so they can think more clearly, make decisions faster, and r educe mental stress during demanding situations. Also Read 7 daily habits that quietly build lasting confidence 4. The Scout Mindset by Julia Galef Galef argues that the best thinkers approach problems with curiosity rather than defensiveness. The book teaches readers how to evaluate situations objectively, challenge assumptions, and make better decisions under pressure. 5. The Courage to Be Disliked by Ichiro Kishimi and Fumitake Koga Based on the ideas of psychologist Alfred Adler, this book explores how people can stop seeking constant approval from others. It offers insights into handling criticism, pressure, and anxiety with greater confidence. 6. Peak Mind by Amishi P. Jha Neuroscientist Amishi Jha explains how attention works and why stress can impair decision-making. The book provides research-backed techniques for improving focus and maintaining clarity during challenging moments. 7. The Extended Mind by Annie Murphy Paul This book challenges the idea that thinking happens only inside our heads. Paul explores how our surroundings, relationships, and physical actions can help us solve problems and make better decisions when under pressure. Final thoughts Pressure has a way of revealing our habits, thought patterns, and emotional responses. While stressful situations cannot always be avoided, our ability to navigate them can improve through practice and learning. These seven books approach the subject from different angles- psychology, philosophy, leadership, history, and personal development- but they share a common lesson: clear thinking under pressure comes from preparation, perspective, and resilience. The more we develop those qualities, the better equipped we become to handle life's most demanding moments.

title: Quantum computing and AI firm QpiAI secures Rs 50 Cr debt financing from InnoVen Capital
content: Quantum computing and artificial intelligence company QpiAI has secured Rs 50 crore in debt financing from InnoVen Capital India Fund II, with the Bengaluru startup allotting 5,000 Series B non-convertible debentures to the fund, according to RoC filings. The debentures have a face value of Rs 1 lakh each, carry a 13.85% annual coupon, and are secured. The transaction was approved by QpiAI’s board on August 28. Entrackr was the first to report the debt financing. The transaction adds debt alongside QpiAI’s earlier equity fundraising. The company had raised $6.5 million in a pre-Series A round in June 2024, led by YourNest and SIDBI Venture Capital, followed by a $32 million Series A in July 2025 led by Avataar Ventures and the National Quantum Mission. That puts its disclosed equity funding at $38.5 million before the latest debt round. Companies typically use venture debt to add capital without issuing new shares, thereby limiting ownership dilution for founders and existing investors. It can also provide additional runway between equity rounds and help finance growth while a company works towards commercial milestones. Also Read QpiAI opens ‘Asia’s largest’ quantum chip foundry, targets 10,000-qubit processors The financing comes as QpiAI pushes further into quantum hardware and software. However, the company has not disclosed a specific use for the Rs 50 crore proceeds in the board resolution; so the funds cannot be tied to a particular project. Founded in 2019, QpiAI develops vertically integrated quantum systems and AI platforms for areas including drug discovery, materials science, manufacturing, logistics and finance. It launched its 25-qubit QpiAI-Indus system in 2025 and subsequently unveiled a 64-qubit processor. The company has previously stated its goal to move quantum technology beyond experimentation and towards commercial use. Founder and CEO Nagendra Nagaraja has said that “markets are ripe for utility-scale quantum computers with logical qubits,” referring to more advanced machines built around error-corrected qubits. The latest financing arrives as India builds policy and infrastructure around emerging technologies. The National Quantum Mission, approved in April 2023 with an outlay of Rs 6,003.65 crore over eight years, is aimed at developing quantum computing, communication, sensing, materials and devices, including intermediate-scale machines with 50 to 1,000 physical qubits.
